land.text: Hami, where Gunashiri broke away from the Northern Yuan in 1389

capitals.name: Hami (Kumul)
capitals.note: The infobox gives Kumul or Hami as the location and no named capital; by 1390 Gunashiri 'had established himself at Hami'.

rulers.name: Gunashiri (Unaširi)
rulers.note: Founder; the page's ruler list (taken from the Japanese Wikipedia list, as WebFetch returned it) gives Unaširi 1380-1393, while the text has him breaking away in 1389 and established at Hami by 1390; the start follows the text.

rulers.name: Engke Temür
rulers.note: List 1393-1405; the English text calls him Gunashiri's successor and has him accept a Ming guard in 1404.

rulers.name: Khalīl sulṭān
rulers.note: List 1439-1457; the page calls him a Northern Yuan vassal 'till 1455'.

rulers.name: Nugandashiri (queen mother)
rulers.note: List 1460-1467; the text has the khan overthrown by a pro-Mongol faction in 1463 and the Ming reinstalling Gunashiri's house from 1467.

rulers.name: Nugandashiri and Bag Temür (rivals)
rulers.note: The list gives the rivalry as 1460-1472 or 1466-1472; the years here run from the end of Nugandashiri's sole listing to Qanshin.

rulers.name: Beyazıt
rulers.note: List 1505-1513; Mansur Khan took Hami in 1513.

correction.text: Hami (Kumul) in Xinjiang, 'a kingdom that existed in Kumul or Hami', ruling a Uyghur population

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives a place, no boundary and no area; Turfan is mentioned only as a place where Buddhism survived, not as Kara Del's territory. The Ming guard of 1404-1406 left the kingdom nominally in place ('did not govern directly or collect taxes').

ledger.note: 1389: Gunashiri breaks away from the Northern Yuan at Hami. 'Founded by the Yuan prince Gunashiri, a descendant of Chagatai Khan, around 1389'; 'In 1389 he broke away from the Northern Yuan'; 'By 1390 he had established himself at Hami and ruled a Uyghur population'.
1391: the Ming occupy Hami and force submission. 'The Ming occupied the territory and forced submission, though Gunashiri kept control'; the kingdom had paid tribute to the Ming since the 1380s.

1404: the occupation becomes a protectorate. 'Engke Temür accepted a Ming guard and Hami became a prefecture. The Ming did not govern directly or collect taxes, and the ruler received the title Zhongshunwang (the obedient prince)'; the Hami Guard is set up by 1406 (the Northern Yuan sometimes kept influence). The ming-dynasty dossier should record the protectorate as a vassal relation from 1404.

1404: the occupation becomes a Ming protectorate. 'In 1404, Gunashiri's successor Engke Temiir accepted the establishment of a Ming guard and became Hami Prefecture'; 'From 1406, it was governed by Ming under the Hami Guard' (the guard itself is 1406). Hami stays a Ming dependant until it 'switched his allegiance from the Chinese Ming Emperor to Mansur Khan' in 1513 (Mansur page). Mirror of the vassal relation that the ming-dynasty dossier should carry with counterpart kara-del.

1445 (bridging, to match the four-oirats dossier /ledger/3): 'During the 1430s, Kara Del submitted to the Oirats' (Kara Del page; the decade is all the page gives); the Kara Del infobox has 'Conquered by Esen of the Northern Yuan' without a year. The four-oirats dossier dates Esen's forcing of Hami to accept Mongol titles to 1445 from the Esen Taishi page (not reopened here); the two dossiers agree on 1445, the page's own date lies in the 1430s.
1446: the protectorate is interrupted by the punitive occupation below ('In 1446, disturbances broke out in Hami'); a bridging pair with the vassal_start that follows the occupation.
1446: Ren Li's Ming force occupies Hami. 'Disturbances led Ming forces under Ren Li to occupy the city and deport 1,230 people east of Jiayuguan.'
1446: the punitive occupation ends in the same expedition; the page gives no end year and has the Ming 'repeatedly' reinstating Gunashiri's house from 1467. A bridging end.

region.text: Hami, back under the Ming guard

ledger.note: 1446: the Ming tie resumes after Ren Li's expedition. The page does not say whether the Ming withdrew, restored the prince or how the episode ended; it has the Ming 'repeatedly' reinstalling Gunashiri's house from 1467 after the 1463 coup, and the prince changing allegiance from the Ming in 1513 (Mansur page). A bridging judgment.

1455: the Oirat (Northern Yuan) overlordship ends with Esen's death. The Kara Del ruler list says the sultan Khalil was a Northern Yuan vassal 'till 1455'; the page names no Oirat end date and no Esen death. Mirror of four-oirats /ledger/6 (c1 there).
1513: Hami leaves the Ming. 'In 1513 the Qara Del prince of Hami [...] switched his allegiance from the Chinese Ming Emperor to Mansur Khan' (Mansur page).

1513: Hami goes to Mansur Khan. 'Mansur Khan, ruler of Moghulistan, conquered Hami, and Kara Del officially converted to Islam'; the Turpan page: 'took Kara Del in 1513'; the Mansur page: the prince 'switched his allegiance from the Chinese Ming Emperor to Mansur Khan'.

region.text: Hami, annexed by the Turpan Khanate

ledger.note: 1513: Kara Del ends. Infobox dates 'c. 1389-1513'; Turfan 'also annexed Hami' (Mansur page).

wars.name: Ming occupation of Hami (Ren Li)
wars.outcome: Ming forces under Ren Li occupied the city and deported 1,230 people east of Jiayuguan.

wars.name: Mansur Khan’s conquest of Hami
wars.outcome: The Kara Del prince changed allegiance from the Ming emperor to Mansur Khan and Hami was annexed by Turfan.

certainty.note: The kingdom is a district round Hami; no boundary is recorded.

sources.title: Kara Del
sources.note: Qamil or Kara Del c.1389-1513: Gunashiri breaks from the Northern Yuan 1389, Hami by 1390, Ming occupation 1391, Hami Guard 1404-1406, Oirat submission 1430s, Ren Li 1446, coup 1463, Ming reinstatements from 1467, Mansur's conquest 1513.

sources.title: Mansur Khan (Moghul Khan)
sources.note: 1513: the Qara Del prince switched allegiance from the Ming emperor to Mansur Khan; Turfan annexed Hami.

notes:
A small Uyghur kingdom at Hami (Kumul), 1389-1513, between the Ming, the Northern Yuan, the Oirats, Turfan and Moghulistan; ia-02-b and ia-02-c flagged it as a missing counterpart (kara-del, 1389-1517 and 1445-1455). Cliopatria has no shape for it; the keyframe is a 120 km circle at Hami because the pages name no boundary.

The Ming relation is a protectorate from 1404 (Hami Guard) that the ming-dynasty dossier (ea) should carry as a vassal relation with counterpart kara-del; the Kara Del page also has the kingdom submitting to the Oirats in the 1430s (a vassal event for four-oirats, undated beyond the decade), a pro-Mongol coup in 1463 and Ming reinstatements from 1467. The end date 1513 is the Kara Del infobox; the Turpan and Mansur pages agree (a change of allegiance in 1513, then annexation by Turfan); ia-02-b's 1517 end is the Ming-Turpan fighting over Hami, which the Mansur page dates to 1517, 1524 and 1528 (see the turpan-khanate dossier). Native name 哈密國 is from the Kara Del infobox.


[Repair ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] Reviewer findings applied after reopening the Kara Del and Mansur Khan pages: (1) vassal_start 1404 and vassal_end 1513 with ming-dynasty (c3), interrupted 1446 by the Ren Li occupation (vassal_end/vassal_start at c1; the page does not say how the occupation ended). (2) Oirat overlordship: vassal_start 1445 (c1, to match four-oirats /ledger/3; the page says 'During the 1430s') and vassal_end 1455 (c2: the ruler list calls Khalil a Northern Yuan vassal 'till 1455'). The four-oirats dossier should use the slug kara-del instead of 'Kara Del (Hami)'. (3) Rulers: the full list of the page replaces the single Gunashiri line; the list is as WebFetch returned it from the Japanese Wikipedia list the page cites and differs from the English text on the first reigns (Unaširi 1380-1393 against the 1389 break-away; Engke Temür 1393-1405 against his 1404 acceptance of the guard). Disagreement kept: the counterpart direction of the vassal events follows the reviewer (the vassal's dossier names the suzerain; the schema text says the counterpart is the vassal).
